checks: Matched 53a240dfcf446f5a:03, §5 equation (6), without importing the separate smooth-cap or signed-response assertions.

For each z, its chosen same-parity representative is in the proposed affine hull, and the midpoint is in P. After translating the affine hull to a linear space the orthogonal projection of the representative is zero, so the normal distance of the midpoint is exactly half the old distance.

Iteration is legitimate because every new midpoint belongs to P and has an available representative. Any positive distance would give infinitely many distinct values among finitely many sites. This also handles rank zero and proves the asserted affine-function consequence.

overlap.comparison: It derives Helly and weighted depth bounds from a midpoint-closed graph, rather than a spanning result for an arbitrary subset meeting each occupied parity.
It uses same-parity midpoint transport to compare measures and preserve their barycenter. It does not assert this affine span for each parity representative set.

readability: Distances are measured to one fixed affine hull, so it is irrelevant that the parity can change along the iteration.
review_method: Independent mathematical proof review of the frozen normalized candidate
summary: Midpoint closure and finiteness give the full affine span of any set meeting every occupied parity.
